load_balancer.specs: Automatic failover, one IPv4 address included

block_storage.notes: 3x synchronous replication, no per-operation fees, IOPS/throughput not published. Attached to K8s workloads via CSI; disks for standalone compute are in preview.

object_storage.notes: API requests and ingress free; outgoing traffic billed at the general €0.025/GB rate. Frankfurt.

egress.notes: Outgoing traffic €0.025/GB across all products, no free allowance published. Ingress free. Outbound NAT included without per-GB NAT charge (page does not say whether NAT traffic is exempt from the egress rate).

notes: enum GmbH (Cologne), production region Frankfurt (enum region code 'fra'), Tier III+ third-party data centre; Berlin region on request. Kubernetes clusters are currently set up on request only; self-service cluster creation is announced for Q4 2026 (enum.co/pricing, 2026-11-01). The gp nodes are priced as Kubernetes worker nodes: the pricing page lists no standalone VMs (standalone compute is only mentioned as 'disks for standalone compute are in preview'), so these are effectively K8s-only prices. Included with Kubernetes: HA control plane (99.9% SLA on the control-plane API), 100 GB disk per node (page does not say whether local or replicated), outbound NAT, IPv6, DNS. Hourly billing, prices in EUR excl. VAT. price_monthly = published hourly x 730; enum's own monthly figures are €44.00 to €1,408.00 (730 h on an unrounded hourly rate), so the file is up to €0.04/month higher. Commitment discounts on every node: 1 year -10%, 2 years -15%, 3 years -20% (not reflected in the prices). GPUs (reserved NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000, Germany) and Models as a Service on request, no public prices. No own org certification yet: ISO 27001 for enum in progress (target Q4 2026), BSI C5 planned for 2027; the DC operator's ISO 27001/9001/EN 50600 cover the facility only. Startup program: up to €100,000 credits for 12 months (enum.co/startups).
